mainEntity.name: Can I eat yoghurt after dental implant surgery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yoghurt is a dairy product and is generally included in the list of foods to avoid in the first 24 to 72 hours following dental implant surgery. This is particularly relevant if you have been prescribed antibiotics, as calcium in dairy can affect how well certain medications are absorbed. Once the dairy-free period has passed and you have completed your course of antibiotics, yoghurt — particularly soft, plain, low-sugar varieties — may be a gentle and nutritionally helpful food to reintroduce. Always confirm the specific timing with your dental team.

mainEntity.name: Why does dairy interact with antibiotics after dental implant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Certain antibiotics, particularly tetracyclines, bind to calcium in dairy products through a process called chelation. This chemical interaction reduces the amount of antibiotic absorbed through the digestive system, potentially making the medication less effective at preventing infection. Even with other antibiotic classes, some clinicians recommend spacing dairy consumption away from medication doses to support optimal absorption. Your pharmacist can advise on the specific interaction for any antibiotics you have been prescribed.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take for a dental implant to heal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Initial healing of the gum tissue following implant surgery typically takes around two to four weeks. However, the deeper process of osseointegration — where the bone fuses with the implant — can take between three and six months, or longer in some cases. Full restoration with a crown or bridge is usually completed once adequate osseointegration has occurred. Healing timelines vary between individuals depending on factors such as bone density, general health, and lifestyle habits. Your dental professional will provide a personalised treatment timeline.

mainEntity.name: What happens if I accidentally eat dairy after a dental implant?

acceptedAnswer.text: In most cases, accidentally consuming a small amount of dairy in the first day or two after surgery is unlikely to cause serious harm. However, if you are taking antibiotics, it may be worth contacting your prescribing dental professional or pharmacist for guidance on how to manage the remainder of your antibiotic course. The greater concern relates to antibiotic effectiveness rather than direct harm to the implant itself. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your dental team.

mainEntity.name: Can I drink milk alternatives such as oat milk after dental implant surgery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in most cases non-dairy milk alternatives such as oat milk, almond milk, or soy milk can be consumed during the dairy-free period following implant surgery, as they do not contain the same calcium compounds found in animal dairy that may interact with certain antibiotics. However, it is worth choosing unsweetened, room-temperature versions to avoid irritating the surgical site. Always check with your dental team if you are uncertain about specific foods or drinks in your post-operative period.

mainEntity.name: Is it normal to experience dry mouth after dental implant surgery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some degree of dry mouth can occur after dental implant surgery. This may be related to breathing through the mouth, the effects of local anaesthetic or sedation, or certain medications. Saliva plays an important role in the oral environment, and reduced flow can temporarily affect the healing conditions around the surgical site. Sipping cool water regularly throughout the day can help. If dry mouth is persistent or accompanied by other symptoms, it is worth mentioning to your dental team at your follow-up visit.
